title: Unify variant sets and standardize auto-layout constraints for data primitives
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate overlapping component variants across buttons, tables, and chart primitives in the Figma library. Normalize auto-layout constraints and spacing tokens to prevent cascades of layout regressions, reduce variant count, and simplify publishing flow for maintainers. Deliver a migration plan that minimizes downstream PR churn and provides a rollback path.
checklist: Inventory existing variants for buttons/tables/charts and identify semantically equivalent states
Propose canonical state names and semantic token mapping (size, density, intent)
Create migration shim components to preserve file references for 2 weeks
Apply auto-layout constraint templates and run QA on responsive table rows
Update Figma library publish notes and change log
Coordinate with frontend team for token name deprecations and codemod plan
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after spike revealed 37% variant duplication across data primitives and inconsistent auto-layout anchors causing row-jump bugs.
2026-02-25 Liam O'Connor: Completed full inventory; attached CSV with 312 component instances and recommended canonical sets. Flagged three table row variants with mixed vertical alignment.
2026-03-01 Design Review: Agreed to standardize on semantic states (default/hover/active/disabled/error) and three density tokens (compact, standard, spacious). Action: Maya to draft token mapping.
2026-03-05 Engineering feedback (Priya Rao): Suggested maintaining legacy spacing tokens for 1 release and providing a codemod. Also requested stable layer naming for snapshot tests.
2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Implemented shim components and created 'autolayout-templates.fig' in Drive. Ran visual QA on 18 pages; found two charts with overflow clipping issues.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Patch PR #8742 opened to rename 24 tokens and add alignment constraints. Next steps: schedule canary publish and coordinate frontend codemod window.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive variant collapse reduces file size and cognitive load but risks breaking references in older feature branches. We opted for a 2-week shim period and codemod to minimize disruption. QA plan includes visual diff snapshots and a rollback branch for publish.
follow_up: Schedule canary publish during low-deploy window (2026-03-18 to 2026-03-20)
Coordinate with PM to announce deprecation in release notes and internal changelog
Create frontend codemod RFC and pair with eng for rollout
Monitor usage analytics for renamed tokens and open a post-mortem if >0.5% of snapshots fail
